newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French August unemployment jumps.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French August unemployment jumps.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on French unemployment which rose 39,500 in August to 3,085,100, giving a record ILO jobless rate of 12.6 percent, up from 12.5 percent in July.

"It's an extraordinary number, quite a shock. It will certainly require more (interest) rate cuts from the Bank of France. Again this is going to raise the gloom and unhappiness in the parliament, we're heading for a tough political weekend."
Valerie Plagnol, economist, Credit Commercial de France:

"It does increase the potential for social tensions when there is little hope for unemployment and these are only August numbers. There were plans to cut more jobs in a number of sectors in September."
"It also means that pickup in household consumption in third quarter won't be supportive for the fourth quarter. The momentum beyond third quarter cannot be assured at all."
"From a market point of view it underlines the need lower interest rates, and it's not so good from a long-term persepective and could help keep the 10-year spread over Germany positive."

"The unemployment number tells us that strong consumption is having little effect on output. It's not a surprise because strong demand is still being met by stocks. We have the view that GDP will rise in the third quarter but not by as much as consumption because of stock adjustment.

Clearly it's important because it comes amid tensions in the government, but as long as Chirac supports Juppe we should not have too much of a political fight. Socially, it doesn't make it easier. But, when people see jobless numbers rising they may be less willing to demand pay rises or strike. It's not clear-cut."
Jean-Louis Mourier, economist, Louis Dreyfus Finance:
"The figures are the reflection of an economy that remains weak. I would expect unemployment to keep edging up to reach around 12.7, 12.8 percent by the end of the year."
